summary: The new version is deployed via its Django migration that adds the customer_note column; existing note values are backfilled into customer_note, and the note column is synced to stay consistent with the new version's writes during the overlap, after which the old version is retired without dropping the note column.
write_consistency: Old version continues writing to note; new version writes to customer_note. After deploy_new a SQL sync stage copies customer_note→note, aligning note with the most recent values from either version. The backfill stage populates customer_note from note for existing rows. Note column remains available for the old version throughout the overlap.
revision_notes: Previous plan failed because the contract SQL stage dropped the note column, causing the runner's smoke test to fail with 'column account_user.note does not exist'. This revision omits the contract stage that drops note, keeping note column throughout. The Django migration on deploy_new creates customer_note, and SQL stages handle data transfer and sync without removing note.

stages.description: Copy every note value from note to customer_note for existing rows.
Sync note column to match customer_note after new version is live, ensuring old version reads latest values.
Retire the old Saleor version. After this stage the old version no longer serves traffic.
